title: alert-correlation-matrix-and-sampling-plan
body:
Purpose:
This doc defines a lightweight "alert correlation matrix" and a pragmatic sampling plan to speed up investigation of performance regressions (latency/throughput/cpu/gpu stalls) in the serving runtime. Goal is consistent, fast first-responses that reduce time-to-blame by providing a prioritized set of signals and a reproducible sampling procedure for traces and canary comparisons.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated clusters backed by the serving runtime (all models).
- Focus is on production alerts and canary deltas that surface p95/p99 regressions or throughput degradations.
- Not a deep profiler guide — this lives earlier in the funnel (collect signals, pick hypothesis, then escalate to full profiling).

Why a matrix?
Alerts come from multiple sources (Grafana thresholds, anomaly detector, SLO burn alerts, console errors). The matrix maps alert types -> likely subsystems -> recommended first-sample artifacts and the triage priority. This reduces noisy back-and-forth when an incident starts.

High-level matrix (represented as rows described here):
- Alert: sudden p99 spike (generation latency) | Likely subsystems: tokenization, attention kernels, kernel fallbacks, memory thrash | First-sample artifacts: 10 representative traces (p99 requests), flamegraph (host & device), kernel logs, model variant tag | Priority: P0
- Alert: sustained throughput drop (requests/sec down 30% over 15m) | Likely subsystems: autoscaler, queueing, batching, GPU saturation | First-sample artifacts: ingestion Q-length histogram, batch-size distribution, host CPU/GPU util timeline (5m), allocation events | Priority: P1
- Alert: increased error rate with latency unchanged | Likely subsystems: decoder bugs, tokenizer errors, model OOMs | First-sample artifacts: error traces, example inputs, model logs, recent deploy rollouts | Priority: P1
- Alert: p95 regression in canary only | Likely subsystems: model variant change, quantization differences, kernel upgrade | First-sample artifacts: canary vs baseline aggregated traces, hot-spot token paths, compilation flags | Priority: P0

Sampling plan (pragmatic rules):
1) First 10 minutes after alert fires: increase trace sampling for affected model(s) to 100% (capture lightweight span + kernel annotations). If not feasible for budget, sample 1:10 but prioritise p99 buckets.
2) Capture: request metadata, token-path histogram, batch-size for every sampled request, and GPU kernel timings when available. Persist to S3/temp-bucket with alert id tag.
3) Canary snapshot: if canary is implicated, take a deploy snapshot (binary+flags) and capture 200 synthetic canary requests that match the slow traffic signature (same prompt length distribution).
4) Retention: keep full traces for 72 hours, aggregated metrics for 90 days (for regressions that emerge slowly).

Quick "bisect-lite" (can be run before a full git bisect):
- Aim: narrow candidate commits or model/infra changes in < 2 hours.
- Inputs: time window for regression start, list of deploys/infra changes, commit history for model/serving bits.
- Steps: A) Compare canary baseline snapshot from just before regression to current canary bundle (requests + aggregated traces). B) If discrepancy large, roll back to immediate prior canary binary in staging and run synthetic load (2000 requests at target qps) and observe p99. C) If rollback restores latency, perform binary half-split: test midpoint commit/build between good and bad. Repeat until candidate commit identified.
- When to stop: when the suspected change is isolated to a single PR or non-code (kernel, compiler flag) change.

Dashboard queries and signal snippets (examples):
- P95 generation time by model: promql: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(generation_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
- Batch size distribution: sum(rate(requests_batched[5m])) by (batch_size, model)
- GPU kernel fallback rate: increase in kernel_fallback_total{kernel="attention"} over 10m
- Latency vs CPU steal: increase in node_cpu_steal_seconds_total correlated with p99 spikes
- Example ELK query to find p99 traces: status:200 AND service:serving-runtime AND duration:[500ms TO *] | top 200 by duration

Trace & instrumentation checklist (quick toggles):
- Enable kernel-level timing (device-side) for sampled traces.
- Turn on prefix/KV cache debug for affected model if cache-hit hypothesis exists.
- Increase token-path logging for 1k requests (strip PII).
- Tag traces with deploy id, model hash, quantization profile.

Canary comparison heuristics (what to look for):
- Token-path divergence: a small fraction of requests taking different decoding routes often indicates tokenization or regex/token map bug.
- Batch shape changes: increased variance in batch sizes + shorter tails usually increase p99 for small requests (due to batching inefficiency).
- Kernel time inflation: device kernel avg increases even when CPU load constant -> likely kernel-level regression (new compiler flags, fused op reorder).
- Memory pressure patterns: repeated allocation/free spikes aligned with latency peaks -> GC/pathological allocator for particular model shapes.

Example incident sketch (realistic):
- 08:07: Grafana alert fires: p99 for text-generation-service spiked from 380ms to 820ms (5m window).
- 08:08: Pager duty acknowledgment, increase trace sampling for model-x to 100% for next 20m.
- 08:12: Quick compare of last canary snapshot shows p99 at 790ms vs baseline 360ms. Batch-size distribution unchanged. Kernel fallback metric increased 6x.
- 08:20: Flamegraphs show attention kernel time doubled. Recent PR notes show kernel optimisation merged 08:01. Rollback of that kernel change to staged binary restores baseline on synthetic run. Root cause: new scheduling heuristic on fused-attention that regresses short sequences.

Common signatures and hypotheses (cheat sheet):
- p99 up but median stable -> variance increase (likely queuing or heterogenous kernel paths).
- median & p99 up proportionally -> global slowdown (resource saturation, network).
- throughput down + latency up -> batching/autoscaler or backpressure.
- errors increase with latency stable -> model decode exception or tokeniser mismatch.

Escalation and handoffs:
- If after 30 minutes: we have candidate commit/flag -> open a focused investigation PR and assign the kernel/serving owner.
- If no candidate after 60 minutes: escalate to oncall SRE + runtime lead for offline profiling.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (small action list):
- Define budget guardrails for 100% trace sampling during peak hours (Priya) 
- Add a lightweight dashboard tile that shows 'recent canary delta score' per model (Maya)
- Automate capture of 200 synthetic canary requests at alert time into a temp snapshot with alert id (Alex)

Next immediate actions (owners):
- Maya: create dashboard tile prototype by 2026-03-20.
- Alex: spike on automated synthetic snapshot capture, add to PR checklist by 2026-03-24.
- Priya: propose trace-sampling cost threshold and alert override play by 2026-03-22.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this lightweight — we want fast heuristics that point at the right domain (kernel vs infra vs model) not exhaustive profiling.
- Share with solutions-eng before wider rollout; their canaries sometimes exercise different prompt distributions.

References and links:

- Perf dashboard templates: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PerfDashboardTemplates

End of doc.
